mal:area.comment: This section details the Common Object Model area; the structures used by the service are detailed in section 4. The area and structures are defined in terms of the MO Message Abstraction Layer (MAL), so it is possible to deploy them over any supported protocol and message transport.
mal:area.name: COM
mal:area.mal:documentation: The instance identifier of an object must not use the value of '0' for actual object instances as this is the wildcard value.
The related field of an object must not use the value of '0' as this is the wildcard value.
The instance identifier of the source field of an object must not use the value of '0' as this is the wildcard value.
If the MAL data type specification is being used the body of an object shall be a concrete type.
If the MAL data type specification is being used the body of an object shall not be an abstract Attribute.
If the MAL data type specification is being used the body of an object shall not be a list.

mal:service.comment:
An event is a specific object representing 'something that happens in the system at a given point in time'. The event service provides a generic mechanism for the distribution of events. An event is a special type of COM object and is identified by the normal object fields (domain, object type, and object instance identifier). It may also contain:
  • a link to a source object (that caused the event to be generated)
  • a link to a service specific related object
  • a body that is specific to the event type and whose data structure is defined by the service that declares the event.
The event service only defines a single operation that supports the publishing of events and subscription of events generated by other components. Events are published with a MAL update type of DELETION. Events are something that happens at a given point in time, therefore they in themselves have no lifetime, they are created and deleted at the time instant in time. For efficiency purposes only the deletion update is used.
mal:service.name: Event
mal:service.mal:documentation: The event service may be used for the publishing and monitoring of COM events.
The identification of the event shall follow the COM object rules.
The COM object source link shall point to the object that caused the event to be generated unless stated otherwise by the defining service specification.
The COM object related link shall be service and event type specific.
When an event is published using the PUBLISH-SUBSCRIBE monitorEvent operation defined in the event service it shall be published with a MAL update type of DELETED.
When an event is published, the COM object instance identifier shall be populated by the publisher.
The object instance identifier should be unique for a domain and object type.
An event may have an associated body that is published with it.
The type and contents of the body of an event shall be specified in the defining service specification but must be a concrete type or an Attribute.
Each type of event is a separate COM object type and therefore may be stored in a COM archive.
When a service implementation requires that the events it generates be persisted, upon event emission, the event shall be stored as normal.
The related link is service specific and shall always be null if not explicitly used by a service.
The source link shall point to the source object of the event.

mal:pubsubIP.comment: The monitorEvent operation allows a consumer to subscribe for events.
mal:pubsubIP.name: monitorEvent
mal:pubsubIP.mal:documentation: The first subscription key shall contain the event object number as a MAL::Long.

The MAL::EntityKey.secondSubKey shall contain the area, service, and version ObjectType fields as a MAL::Long populated as (in hex) 0xAAAASSSSVVXXXXXX where AAAA is the area (16 bits), SSSS is the service (16 bits), VV is the version (8 bits), and XXXXXX is unused and set to zero (24 bits). For example, for an area of '1', and a service of '2', and a version of '3' the field would contain (in hex) 0x0001000203000000.
The MAL::EntityKey.thirdSubKey shall contain the event object instance identifier.

The MAL::EntityKey.fourthSubKey shall contain the area, service, version and number fields of the event source ObjectType using same methodology as given for the second sub key but replacing the XXXXXX part with the number field.
The related and source links of the event shall populate the ObjectLinks part of the publish/notify message.
The body of the event shall populate the final part of the publish/notify message.
The timestamp of the Event shall be taken from the publish message.
An event in one domain may be generated by something in another domain therefore the domain of the event shall not be required to be the same domain as the source of the event.

mal:field.name: eventObjectNumber
mal:field.comment: The event object number.

mal:field.name: K2
mal:field.comment: The area, service and version fields of the event object type.

mal:field.name: K3
mal:field.comment: The event object instance identifier.

mal:field.name: K4
mal:field.comment: The area, service, version and number fields of the event source object type.
The object links of the event.
mal:field.name: eventLinks

mal:field.comment: The body of the event.
mal:field.name: eventBody

com:archiveUsage.comment: The events may be persisted in a COM archive.

mal:service.comment: The Archive service provides a basic interface to a standard archiving function. It follows the basic CRUD principles and allows simple querying of the archive. It provides operations to add new objects to an archive, delete objects from an archive, update existing objects in an archive, and also query the content of the archive. The query operation provides a basic querying ability, allowing a consumer to filter on fields from the object headers (such as domain etc) and also filter on the body of the object if it uses the MAL data type specification. The query operation is extensible but the extensions would be outside this standard. Finally, a consumer of the archive can monitor it for changes by subscribing for archive events from the event service. Any change to the archive is published using the event service if it is supported by an implementation.
mal:service.name: Archive

mal:invokeIP.comment: Retrieves a set of objects identified by their object instance identifier.
mal:invokeIP.name: retrieve
mal:invokeIP.mal:documentation: If any of the fields of the object type contains the wildcard value of '0' then an INVALID error shall be returned.
If the domain contains the wildcard value of '*' then an INVALID error shall be returned.
If the object instance identifier list contains the wildcard value '0' then all object instances shall be matched.
If any explicitly requested object cannot be matched then an UNKNOWN error shall be returned.
The response shall contain the set of matched objects.
The objBodies shall be ordered identically to the metadata list unless no body for the object is declared in the service specification, in which case a NULL replaces the complete list.
There shall be an entry in both metadata and objBodies for each matched object.
When no objects have been matched only a response with NULL for both metadata and objBodies shall be returned.
The ordering of the returned objects is not specified and implementation specific.
If ordering of the returned objects is required then the query operation should be used instead.

mal:field.name: objType
mal:field.comment: The type of the object to be retrieved.

mal:field.name: domain
mal:field.comment: The domain of the object to be retrieved.

mal:field.name: objInstIds
mal:field.comment: The list of ids to be retrieved.

mal:field.name: metadata
mal:field.comment: The metadata of the matched objects.

mal:field.name: objBodies
mal:field.comment: The bodies of the matched objects.

mal:errorRef.comment: The request contains a wildcard value in either the object type field or the domain.
One or more of the requested objects specified in the operation do not exist and therefore cannot be found.

mal:extraInformation.comment: A list of the indexes of the error values shall be contained in the extra information field.

mal:progressIP.comment: Retrieves a set of ids, and optionally the object bodies, from a list of supplied queries. The PROGRESS interaction pattern is used as the returned set of data may be quite large and this allows it to be split over several MAL messages.
mal:progressIP.name: query
mal:progressIP.mal:documentation: If the returnBody field is set to TRUE, then the body of the objects shall be returned otherwise only the ObjectType and ArchiveDetails shall be returned and the returned list of the bodies of the objects shall be replaced with a NULL.
Each part of the object type may contain the wildcard value of '0'.
A single query shall be formed by the combination of an ArchiveQuery from the archiveQuery list and a QueryFilter from the queryFilter list.
If a query does not contain a QueryFilter part then that entry in the QueryFilter list shall be replaced with a NULL value.
If the request does not contain any QueryFilters then the complete list may be replaced with a NULL.
The size of the archiveQuery and queryFilter lists must be the same unless the complete queryFilter list is replaced with a NULL otherwise an INVALID error shall be raised.
For each query, the ArchiveQuery and the QueryFilter shall contain the COM object fields to filter on.
The ArchiveQuery may contain the wildcard value of NULL on each of the fields.
If an ArchiveQuery contains an end time but no start time then it shall match the single object that has a timestamp closest to, but not greater than, the end time field.
The end time field may specify a time in the future.
If the sortFieldName of the ArchiveQuery does not reference a defined field then an INVALID error shall be returned.
Each query shall be evaluated separately from each other, the filter of one query will not affect the filter of another. This forms a logical OR operation.
If the QueryFilter contains an error then an INVALID error shall be returned. The definition of erroneous values are filter specific and defined in the relevant filter structure specification.
The updates shall contain the set of matched objects.
If a wildcard was used in the ObjectType part of the request then the updates shall contain the ObjectType of each matched object.
If there was not any wildcards in the ObjectType part of the request the ObjectType in the updates shall be replaced by a NULL.
The domain field in each Update message shall contain the domain of the objects being returned.
If multiple ObjectTypes or domains have been matched then multiple Update messages may be returned.
In each Update message there shall be an entry in both objDetails and objBodies for each matched object.
The objDetails field in each Update message shall contain the archive details stored for the matched objects.
If the returnBody field of the request was TRUE, the objBodies field in each Update message shall contain the bodies of the objects.
If the returnBody field of the request was NULL or FALSE, the objBodies field in each Update message shall be replaced by a NULL.
The returned lists shall be sorted based on the sorting options specified in ArchiveQuery.
Each domain/object type pair shall be sorted separately from other domain/object type pairs, there is no requirement for sorting to be applied across domain/object type pairs.

When the field being sorted on contains a NULL value, or does not exist in the matched object (due to a containing composite being NULL), these entries shall be added to the end of the returned list in the order that they are matched.
The final Response message shall be empty and signals to the consumer that all matched objects have been returned.
When no objects have been matched, only this empty Response is sent with no preceding Update messages.

mal:field.name: returnBody
mal:field.comment: Flag that defines if the body is to be returned.

mal:field.name: objType
mal:field.comment: The type of the object to be returned.

mal:field.name: archiveQuery
mal:field.comment: The archive query.

mal:field.name: queryFilter
mal:field.comment: The query filter.

mal:field.name: objType
mal:field.comment: The type of the matched object.

mal:field.name: domain
mal:field.comment: The domain of the matched objects.

mal:field.name: objDetails
mal:field.comment: The archive details of the matched objects.

mal:field.name: objBodies
mal:field.comment: The bodies of the matched objects, or NULL if not requested.

mal:errorRef.comment: One or more of the query filters supplied contains an invalid value.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The extra information field contains a list of the indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list supplied.

mal:invokeIP.comment: Counts the set of objects based on a supplied query.
mal:invokeIP.name: count
mal:invokeIP.mal:documentation: The ObjectType, ArchiveQuery and QueryFilter parts of the request shall be populated exactly the same as for the query operation.
The response shall contain the count of matched objects.
There shall be an entry in the counts list for each entry in the archiveQuery list.
The counts list shall be ordered the same as the archiveQuery and queryFilter lists so that the response can be matched to the corresponding request.

mal:field.name: objType
mal:field.comment: The type of the object.
The archive query.
mal:field.name: archiveQuery

mal:field.comment: The query filter.
mal:field.name: queryFilter
counts
mal:field.comment: The number of entries found that match the provided criteria.

mal:errorRef.comment: One or more of the query filters supplied contains an invalid value.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The extra information field contains a list of the indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list supplied.

mal:requestIP.comment: Stores new objects in the archive and causes an ObjectStored event to be published by the archive. When new objects are being stored in an archive by a service provider the archive service provider is capable of allocating an unused object instance identifier for the objects being stored. The returned object instance identifier should be used by the service provider for identifying the object instances to its consumer to ensure that only a single object instance identifier is used for each object instance.
mal:requestIP.name: store
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The returnObjInstIds field indicates whether the operation should return the ids used, if TRUE it shall return them, otherwise it returns NULL.
If the object instance identifier supplied in the archive details is set to 0 then the store operation shall allocate a new and unused object instance identifier.

If the object instance identifier supplied in the archive details is not set to 0 and is currently used in the archive then a DUPLICATE error is returned and no objects from the request shall be stored.

The objDetails and objBodies lists must be the same size as there is only one entry in each for each object to be stored. If they differ in size an INVALID error is returned with the extra error information integer giving the index of the list entry without a matching entry in the other list.
An INVALID error shall be returned if a wildcard value of '0' is used in the object type.
An INVALID error shall be returned if a wildcard value of '*' is used in the domain identifier list.
An INVALID error shall be returned if the values of '0', '*', or NULL are used in the network, timestamp or provider fields of the archive details except for the object instance identifier.
The type of the body of the object should be checked against the declared type in the relevant service specification, if different an INVALID error is raised.
If any error is returned then the store operation shall be rolled back and nothing is stored as a result of the operation.
The response shall contain the set of new ids if the returnObjInstIds field was TRUE, otherwise it returns NULL.
The objInstIds list shall be ordered identically to the submitted objDetails list so that the returned ids can be mapped to the correct objects.

mal:field.comment: Flag that states if the ids are to be returned.
mal:field.name: returnObjInstIds

mal:field.comment: The type of the objects to be stored.
mal:field.name: objType

mal:field.comment: The domain of the objects to be stored.
mal:field.name: domain

mal:field.comment: The list of archive details for the objects to be stored.
mal:field.name: objDetails

mal:field.comment: The list of object bodies to be stored.
mal:field.name: objBodies

mal:field.comment: The list of ids of the stored objects.
mal:field.name: objInstIds

mal:errorRef.comment: One or more of the objects being stored has supplied an object instance identifier that is already in use in the archive.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The extra information field contains a list of the indexes of the erroneous values from the originating request list.

mal:errorRef.comment: One or more of the objects being stored contains an invalid value.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The extra information field contains a list of the indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list supplied.

mal:submitIP.comment: Updates an object (or set of objects), causes an ObjectUpdated event to be published by the archive.
mal:submitIP.name: update
mal:submitIP.mal:documentation: The object instance identifier contained in the ArchiveDetails, combined with the object type and domain from the request, shall be used to match objects.
If requested object cannot be matched then an UNKNOWN error shall be returned and nothing will be updated.
The remainder of the ArchiveDetails shall be used to update the matched objects.
No wildcard values shall be accepted in the object type, the domain, and the object instance identifier, an INVALID error is returned in this case and no objects are updated.

mal:field.name: objType
mal:field.comment: The type of the object.
The domain of the objects to be updated.
mal:field.name: domain

mal:field.comment: The list of archive details for the objects to be updated.
mal:field.name: objDetails

mal:field.comment: The list of updated object bodies.
mal:field.name: objBodies

mal:errorRef.comment: One or more of the requested objects specified in the operation do not exist and therefore cannot be found.

mal:extraInformation.comment: A list of the indexes of the error values shall be contained in the extra information field.

mal:errorRef.comment: One or more of the objects being updated contains a wildcard value in the object identifier fields.

mal:extraInformation.comment: The extra information field contains a list of the indexes of the erroneous values from the originating list supplied.

mal:requestIP.comment: Deletes an object (or set of objects) and causes an ObjectDeleted event to be published by the archive.
mal:requestIP.name: delete
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The objType field shall contain the type of object to match and is not permitted to contain the wildcard value.
The domain field shall contain the domain of the objects to match and is not permitted to contain the wildcard value.
If either the objType or domain field contains a wildcard value then an INVALID error shall be returned and no object deleted.
If the object instance identifier list contains the wildcard value '0' then all object instances shall be matched.
If any explicitly requested object cannot be matched then an UNKNOWN error shall be returned and nothing will be deleted.
The matched objects shall be deleted from the archive.
The response shall contain the set of ids of the deleted objects.

mal:field.comment: The type of the object.
mal:field.name: objType

mal:field.comment: The domain of the objects to be deleted.
mal:field.name: domain

mal:field.comment: The list of ids of the objects to be deleted.
mal:field.name: objInstIds

mal:field.comment: The ids of the deleted objects.
mal:field.name: deletedObjInstIds

mal:errorRef.comment: One or more of the requested objects specified in the operation do not exist and therefore cannot be found.

mal:extraInformation.comment: A list of the indexes of the error values shall be contained in the extra information field.

mal:errorRef.comment: The supplied object type or domain contains a wildcard value.

com:events.comment: For each stored object, an 'ObjectStored' event may be published to the event service. For each updated object, an 'ObjectUpdated' event may be published to the event service. For each deleted object, an 'ObjectDeleted' event may be published to the event service. The source link of the generated events shall link to the object being stored/updated/deleted. Archive service events shall be persisted silently in order not to trigger an infinite event loop.

com:event.comment: For each stored object, an event of type 'ObjectStored' may be published to the event service.
com:event.name: ObjectStored

com:sourceObject.comment: The Object source is the newly stored object.

com:event.comment: For each updated object, an event of type 'ObjectUpdated' may be published to the event service.
com:event.name: ObjectUpdated

com:sourceObject.comment: The Object source is the updated object.

com:event.comment: For each deleted object, an event of type 'ObjectDeleted' may be published to the event service.
com:event.name: ObjectDeleted

com:sourceObject.comment: The Object source is the deleted object.

mal:service.comment: The ArchiveSync service allows a service consumer to synchronize the COM Archive with a service provider.
mal:service.name: ArchiveSync

mal:requestIP.comment: The getTime operation allows a consumer to retrieve the current time and the time of the last synchronization from the provider.
mal:requestIP.name: getTime

mal:field.comment: The current time on the provider.
mal:field.name: currentTime

mal:field.comment: The time of the last synchronization, or NULL if never synchronized.
mal:field.name: lastSyncTime

mal:progressIP.comment: The retrieveRange operation allows a consumer to retrieve COM archive objects within a specified time range. The response is streamed as a sequence of compressed chunks.
mal:progressIP.name: retrieveRange

mal:field.comment: The start time of the range to retrieve.
mal:field.name: from

mal:field.comment: The end time of the range to retrieve.
mal:field.name: until

mal:field.comment: The list of object types to retrieve, or NULL for all types.
mal:field.name: objectTypes

mal:field.comment: The compression algorithm identifier, or NULL for no compression.
mal:field.name: compression

mal:field.comment: The ticket identifier assigned to this retrieval transaction.

mal:progressIP.comment: The retrieveRangeAgain operation allows a consumer to re-request chunks that were not received in a previous retrieveRange interaction.

mal:field.comment: The ticket identifier from the previous retrieveRange interaction.
mal:field.name: interactionTicket

mal:field.comment: The list of chunk indexes that were not received and need to be retransmitted.
mal:field.name: missingIndexes

mal:field.comment: A chunk of the serialized archive data.

mal:requestIP.comment: The getDictionary operation allows a consumer to retrieve dictionary words by their identifiers.
mal:requestIP.name: getDictionary

mal:field.comment: The list of word identifiers to retrieve from the dictionary.
mal:field.name: wordIds

mal:field.comment: The list of words corresponding to the requested identifiers.
mal:field.name: words

mal:submitIP.comment: The free operation allows a consumer to release a transaction after completing a retrieval.
mal:submitIP.name: free

mal:field.comment: The ticket identifier of the transaction to be released.

mal:errorRef.comment: The provided transaction ticket is unknown.

com:objects.comment: The ArchiveSync service can store the last synchronizations information on the COM Archive.

mal:service.name: Directory
mal:service.comment: The Directory service allows providers to publish information about which services they provide and consumers to discover provider address and capability information. Service provider information is made available using the Directory service add operation and removed using the remove operation. The lookup operation provides the ability for consumers to query the directory service based on a filter such as required service capability. Finally, a provider may supply its set of service specification XML files when publishing its capabilities. This allows consumers that are able to process MO service XML files obtain the files for further processing. It is expected that this would be used to either ensure that no modifications have been made by a provider to a standard service or, in the case of a consumer that is able to dynamically interact with new service specifications, obtain the service specification to allow interaction with that new service.
mal:service.mal:documentation:
The directory service shall provide the capability to:
  1. request provider details based on a filter;
  2. add new provider details;
  3. remove provider details;
  4. request the area XML for a certain MAL area.
A provider shall use the add operation to make available the set of services and the capabilities of those services that it offers.
The add operation shall take a PublishDetails structure which defines the capabilities and addressing information of that provider.
It shall be possible for a provider to offer multiple service addresses and bindings in order to allow the provider to support multiple message transports and encodings.

Each service address entry shall include the service interface binding signature description, interface address, MAL protocol mapping, message encoding, the supported QoS levels and associated QoS properties available for that connection.
A service consumer indicates its required QoS level and priority by using these values in the lookup operation.

For services that have operations based on the PUB-SUB interaction pattern there may be required a separate URI for the broker component. To support this the Directory service shall hold two URIs for each service, the URI of the primary interface and also the URI of the broker.
A ServiceProvider object represents a provider. The COM object body shall hold the provider id taken from the providerId field of the PublishDetails composite.
The ServiceProvider COM object related link shall not be used and therefore set to NULL.
The ServiceProvider COM object source link shall not be used and therefore shall be set to NULL.
A ProviderCapabilities object represents the supported capabilities of a provider. The COM object body shall hold the provider details of the provider.
The ProviderCapabilities COM object related link shall indicate which ServiceProvider COM object it links to.
The ProviderCapabilities COM object source link shall not be used and therefore set to NULL.
ServiceProvider and ProviderCapabilities objects shall be created by the add operation.
The object instance identifier for the ServiceProvider and ProviderCapabilities objects shall be populated by the provider of the directory service.
All directory objects must be stored in the COM archive by the provider of the Directory service if the implementation of the Directory service uses a COM archive.

mal:requestIP.name: lookup
mal:requestIP.comment: The lookup operation retrieves the list of providers made available in the Directory service.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: A consumer shall send the lookup criteria to the provider for the providers intended to be retrieved.
The various filters that may be specified as part of this operation shall be combined using AND logic.
The returned list holds the list of providers that match the requested criteria.
If no match is found, then the returned list shall be empty.
If the serviceProviderId field is NULL then all provider identifiers shall be matched.

If the final identifier of the domain field of the filter is the wildcard '*', then all sub-domains shall be searched for matches. If the wildcard is used in any other part of the domain other than the final one then an INVALID error shall be returned.
If the domain field is NULL then all domains shall be matched.
If the network field is NULL then all networks shall be matched.
If the sessionName field is NULL then all session names shall be matched.
The ServiceId field shall be used to match against ServiceId fields held in the PublishDetails used to publish a specific provider.
If the ServiceId field is NULL then all areas, services and versions shall be matched.
If the area field is the wildcard '0' then all areas names shall be matched.
If the service field is the wildcard '0' then all services shall be matched.
If the version field is the wildcard '0' then all area versions shall be matched.
If the requiredCapabilitySets field is NULL or an empty list then all service capability sets shall be matched.
If no providers match the supplied filter then an empty list shall be returned.

mal:field.name: filter
mal:field.comment: The lookup query filter to be used to match the providers.

mal:field.name: matchingProviders
mal:field.comment: The providers that matched the filter.

mal:errorRef.comment: Invalid domain filter value.

mal:requestIP.name: add
mal:requestIP.comment: The add operation adds a new or updates an existing entry in the list of providers held in the directory service.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: If any of the fields of the newProviderDetails domain/sessionName/network fields are either empty or contain the wildcard '*' an INVALID error shall be returned.
If the providerId field of the PublishDetails structure is empty or contains the wildcard '*' an INVALID error shall be returned.
For each contained ServiceId structure if the area/service/version fields contain '0' then an INVALID error shall be returned.
For each contained supportedCapabilitySets list if the list is empty or contains '0' then an INVALID error shall be returned.

If the supportedLevels list is empty or the priorityLevels field is '0' for each contained AddressDetails structure found either within the ProviderDetails or the inner ServiceCapability structures then an INVALID error shall be returned.
If an error is being returned then no changes shall be made.

If the providerId field of the PublishDetails structure matches an existing ServiceProvider COM object, the operation shall update the existing details of that provider. If the providerId field of the PublishDetails structure does not match an existing ServiceProvider COM object, then the operation shall create a new ServiceProvider COM object to represent the new provider.
A new ProviderCapabilities COM object shall be created to store the capabilities of the provider.
The created objects should be stored in the COM archive by the directory provider.
The operation shall return the COM ids of the ServiceProvider and ProviderCapabilities COM objects representing the provider.

mal:field.name: newProviderDetails
mal:field.comment: The details of the provider to be added or updated in the Directory service.

mal:field.name: providerObjId
mal:field.comment: The identifier of the provider.

mal:errorRef.comment: Submitted values are invalid.

mal:submitIP.name: remove
mal:submitIP.comment: The remove operation removes an existing entry from the list of providers held in the Directory service. If no match is found for the withdraw request, then nothing is changed.
mal:submitIP.mal:documentation: If the supplied identifier is '0' an INVALID error shall be returned.
If the supplied identifier does not match an existing ServiceProvider COM object then an UNKNOWN error shall be returned.
If an error is being returned then no changes shall be made.
The matched provider shall be removed from the directory service.

mal:field.name: providerObjId
mal:field.comment: The object instance identifier for the provider to remove from the Directory service.

mal:errorRef.comment: Provider to withdraw was not found.
Submitted values are invalid.

mal:requestIP.name: getAreaXML
mal:requestIP.comment: The getAreaXML operation returns the list of XML files with the information about the area.

mal:field.name: filename
mal:field.comment: The filename of the XML file. The wildcard may be used to return all XML files.

mal:field.name: xmlFiles
mal:field.comment: The list of XML files.

mal:errorRef.comment: Submitted values are invalid.
Provider was not found.

com:objects.comment: The ServiceProvider and ProviderCapabilities objects used by the Directory service.

com:archiveUsage.comment: The Directory service COM archive usage.

mal:service.name: Login
mal:service.comment: The Login service defines the primary mechanism for the submission of authentication credentials to a deployment specific security system. It supports operations to allow a user to login, logout, and report available roles. The service is closely tied to the Access Control aspect of the MAL where the returned authentication identifiers are used in the MAL message header to authenticate and authorise message via Access Control. The login service supports the concept of roles, where users may log in with a specific role; the meaning of each role is mission-specific, however it is expected that a specific role allocates the user privileges to invoke operations on mission operation services. The use of login roles is optional but if they are used then the role details are held in the COM archive and the COM archive operations are used to manage the role definitions. The responsibility for maintenance of the login roles is outside the scope of this specification as it is a deployment issue to define the possible roles and associate users to those roles. The form in which the password is sent to the Login provider must be agreed upon beforehand and is dependent on the security system deployed. For example, most security implementations do not recommend the use of plain text passwords but rather some encrypted version of the password. For this reason the contents of the messages sent between the login service consumer and provider during authentication handshaking are implementation-specific.
mal:service.mal:documentation:
The login service shall provide the capability:
  1. log in;
  2. log out;
  3. report the list of possible roles for a login profile.
Instances of a user login shall be represented as LoginInstance COM object.
Instances of a user role shall be represented as LoginRole COM object.
LoginInstance objects shall be created by the login operation.
The object instance identifier for a LoginInstance object shall be populated by the provider of the Login service.
The LoginInstance object shall use the related link to indicate which LoginRole (if any) the login uses.
If a LoginInstance object was created during a login operation then the source link shall be set to NULL.
When a user logs in a LoginEvent COM event shall be generated.
When a user logs out a LogoutEvent COM event shall be generated.
The LoginEvent event shall use the related link to indicate which LoginInstance object is being logged in.
The LogoutEvent event shall use the related link to indicate which LoginInstance object is being logged out.
The LoginEvent event shall not use the COM object source link and shall set it to NULL.
The LogoutEvent event shall use the source link to indicate which LoginEvent event it is logging out.
The events shall be published using the COM event service.
LoginInstance objects should be stored in the COM archive.
When a login service event is published, the event object should be stored in the COM archive by the Login provider.
LoginRole objects should be stored in the COM archive.
The COM archive service should be used for maintaining the LoginRole objects.

mal:requestIP.name: login
mal:requestIP.comment: The login operation allows a user to log in to the system. A user can log in more than once by using a different role; however, a specific deployment may place limits on the number of users that may use a specific role, and in that case will fail the login operation with the TOO_MANY error.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: The authenticationId field of the REQUEST message must be NULL otherwise an INVALID error shall be returned.
The authenticationId field shall be checked before applying all other tests here.
The userDetails field shall contain the details of the new user and role combination.
If the username field of the supplied Profile structure is either the wildcard '*' or empty an INVALID error shall be returned.
If roles are required by the system and the role field of the supplied Profile structure is NULL then an INVALID error shall be returned.
If roles are not used by the system the role field of the supplied Profile structure shall be ignored and may be set to NULL.
An UNKNOWN error shall be returned if the username, password and role combination are not correct for the system i.e. unknown user/role or incorrect password.
A DUPLICATE error shall be returned if the username and role combination is currently in use.
A TOO_MANY error shall be returned if the username or role are already used and exceed (deployment dependent) maximum number of concurrent logins/roles.
If the login is successful the provider shall create a new LoginInstance COM object and store it in the COM archive.
The related link of the new LoginInstance COM object shall be set to the requested LoginRole COM object.
A LoginEvent COM event shall be generated at this point.
The returned authId field shall be used as the authenticationId field in future MAL messages by the consumer MAL for authentication. The token is specific to the user and role in use.

mal:field.name: userDetails
mal:field.comment: The details of the user.

mal:field.name: password
mal:field.comment: The password of the user.

mal:field.name: authId
mal:field.comment: The authentication identifier for the user and role.

mal:field.name: objInstId
mal:field.comment: The LoginInstance COM object instance identifier created by the login operation.

mal:errorRef.comment: Username/role combination currently in use.
Submitted profile contains invalid values. No further information is provided as it may compromise security.
Role concurrent session limit count exceeded.
Unknown username/role/password combination.

mal:submitIP.name: logout
mal:submitIP.comment: The logout operation allows a user to log out from the system. No information is passed in the message as the MAL authentication Id is enough to identify the login.
mal:submitIP.mal:documentation: A logged in user shall be matched using the supplied authenticationId.
A LogoutEvent COM event shall be generated at this point.
No errors shall be returned by this operation.

mal:requestIP.name: listRoles
mal:requestIP.comment: The listRoles operation returns the list of available roles for a specific user. This operation is expected to be called before a user logs in so that the software can provide a list of possible roles.
mal:requestIP.mal:documentation: If the username field is either the wildcard '*', NULL or empty an INVALID error shall be returned.

It should be noted that this operation requires both a username and password field before returning any information, this is to ensure that it does not provide a security attack vector by allowing the discovery of valid usernames without first knowing the correct password.
An UNKNOWN error shall be returned if the username and password combination are not correct for the system i.e. unknown user or incorrect password.
The operation shall return a list of LoginRole ids that are permitted for the user or NULL if roles are not used by the system.

mal:field.name: username
mal:field.comment: The username field shall hold the details of the user.

mal:field.name: password
mal:field.comment: The password for the selected username.

mal:field.name: permittedRoles
mal:field.comment: The list of roles.

mal:errorRef.comment: Unknown username/password combination.
Submitted profile contains invalid values.

com:object.comment: The body of the LoginRole object is the role name Identifier.

mal:service.name: Configuration
mal:service.comment: The Configuration service allows a service consumer to activate pre-defined configurations of a provider. The service uses a COM object to represent the different configurations allowed by a provider; a service consumer selects one configuration to activate using the Configuration service activate operation. The contents of a configuration for a provider is deployment specific however the management of these configurations, and the selection of a configuration for current use, is the purpose of this service. Implementations of this service may also use bespoke methods for configuration representation (such as hard-coded configuration) which is outside the scope of this specification, however, the status and management of these configurations can still be managed with this service. NOTE: This service uses the COM Event service to distribute changes in state, therefore participating providers should ensure they are all using the same shared COM Event service if they wish to receive Configuration service events.
mal:service.mal:documentation: The object body of the ServiceConfiguration COM object shall hold the service key that identifies the service it is a configuration of.
The ServiceConfiguration COM object related link shall link to the ConfigurationObjects COM object that contains the objects that form the service configuration.
If the ServiceConfiguration represents a Hard-coded configuration for a single service then the related link shall be set to NULL.
The object body of the ProviderConfiguration COM object shall hold an identifier to identify the provider configuration.
The ProviderConfiguration COM object related link shall link to the ConfigurationObjects COM object that contains the objects that form the provider configuration.
If the ProviderConfiguration represents a Hard-coded configuration for a provider then the related link shall be set to NULL.
The object body of the ConfigurationObjects COM object shall hold a configuration object details structure that links to the objects that form the configuration.
The ConfigurationObjects COM object related link shall be set to NULL.
A ConfigurationStored COM event shall be raised when a configuration has been stored.
The ConfigurationStored COM event body shall hold the ObjectId of the new Configuration object if the store was successful, otherwise NULL for failure.
The ConfigurationStored COM event source link shall be NULL.

Configuration definition objects (ServiceConfiguration, ProviderConfiguration, ConfigurationObjects) must be stored in the COM archive by the provider of the Configuration service if the implementation of the Configuration service uses a COM archive.

The COM objects that hold the actual configuration definition details must be stored in the COM archive by the provider of the relevant service if the implementation of the Configuration service uses a COM archive.
When a ConfigurationStored event is published, the event object should be stored in the COM archive.

com:objects.comment: The ServiceConfiguration, ProviderConfiguration, and ConfigurationObjects COM objects used by the Configuration service.

com:events.comment: The ConfigurationStored event used by the Configuration service.

com:archiveUsage.comment: The Configuration service COM archive usage.

mal:field.comment: Only the objects whose domain matches the provided domain will be returned. The domain field supports the wildcard value of '*' only in the last part of the domain. If NULL then all domains shall be matched.

mal:field.comment: If set to TRUE then returned values shall be sorted in ascending order, if FALSE then in descending order. If NULL then no sorting shall be applied.

mal:field.comment: If the returned values are to be sorted because the sortOrder field is not NULL then this field may contain the name of the field in the object body (MAL::Composite) to sort against. If the object body is not a composite but an Attribute or Enumeration then to sort on the values an empty string of "" should be used. Enumerations are sorted on their ordinal. If this field is NULL then the objects shall be sorted on the COM object timestamp. The field follows the naming convention of CompositeFilter::fieldName. If the field points to a composite, list, abstract type (including Attribute) or Blob then no sorting shall be applied.

mal:composite.name: CompositeFilter
mal:composite.comment: The CompositeFilter allows an archive query to specify a filter based on the content of the body of an object if that body is specified using the MAL data type specification.

mal:field.comment: The name of the field in the object body (MAL::Composite) to match against. It is specified by referring to the name of the field. If the field does not exist in the Composite then the filter shall evaluate to false. If the field is nested inside another Composite, it can be referenced by separating the field names by a '.' character; for example the field 'instId' or the source of an ArchiveDetails composite would be referenced using "details.source.key.instId". If the body is not a Composite but an Attribute or Enumeration then it can be referred to by using a blank ("") string value here. Accessing values from lists is not supported by this method.
mal:field.name: fieldName

mal:field.comment: The type of the filter to apply.
mal:field.name: type

mal:field.comment: The value to compare with. The type of the suppied value and the matched field mst be the same. Must not contain NULL for expression operators CONTAINS, ICONTAINS, GREATER, GREATER_OR_EQUAL, LESS, or LESS_OR_EQUAL otherwise an INVALID error should be returned. Must contain a UInteger ordinal value if the field being matched is an Enumeration. Blob fields can only be used with EQUAL/DIFFER. Must contain a String value if operator is CONTAINS or ICONTAINS otherwise an INVALID error should be returned.
